name: E. Pira & Figli (Chiara Boschis) Barolo Via Nuova 2012
text:
## E. Pira & Figli (Chiara Boschis) Barolo Via Nuova 2012

**The story.** Chiara Boschis was born into [Barolo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barolo): her ancestors founded the Giacomo Borgogno estate in the village in 1761, and her family ran it until its sale in 2008. The expectation was that her brothers would run the winery while she married. She had other plans. In 1980 the legendary Gigi Pira, owner of the E. Pira winery in Barolo, died without heirs; his sisters, friends of the Boschis family, asked them for help, and in 1981 Chiara, still a student in Turin, persuaded her parents to take out a mortgage and buy the [E. Pira cantina](https://www.google.com/maps?q=E.+Pira+e+Figli,+Via+Vittorio+Veneto,+Barolo,+Italy&t=k) and its vineyards ([Skurnik Wines](https://www.skurnik.com/e-pira-chiara-boschis-now-a-family-affair/)).

By 1990 she was running it herself. After tasting and travelling with Giorgio Rivetti and the "Barolo Boys", the modernists of the day, she broke with her family's centuries of tradition: green harvesting, shorter fermentations and small French [barriques](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oak_%28wine%29). Her very first wine, the 1990 Barolo Riserva Cannubi, won the [Gambero Rosso](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gambero_Rosso)'s Tre Bicchieri. Skurnik calls her "rock star, rebel, feminist, pioneer"; she was the first woman winemaker in the Langhe, and ran the estate essentially alone for twenty years. In 2010 her brother Giorgio, his wife and their three daughters joined her ([Skurnik Wines](https://www.skurnik.com/e-pira-chiara-boschis-now-a-family-affair/)).

**The wine: Via Nuova.** "Via Nuova" means "new road". Until the late 2000s it was simply another name for the Terlo vineyard. When Giorgio arrived, Chiara bought old vines in the Mosconi cru at [Monforte d'Alba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monforte_d'Alba) and small parcels at Ravera di Monforte, Le Coste di Monforte, and Gabutti and Baudana in [Serralunga d'Alba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serralunga_d'Alba), and from 2010 Via Nuova became a classic multi-vineyard Barolo blending all her holdings except Cannubi ([Skurnik Wines](https://www.skurnik.com/e-pira-chiara-boschis-now-a-family-affair/)). Antonio Galloni lists the parts as Terlo, Liste, Gabutti, Baudana, Ravera and young vines in Mosconi ([Saratoga Wine](https://www.saratogawine.com/product/e-pira-figli-chiara-boschis-barolo-via-nuova-2010-750ml/)): a tour of the appellation in one bottle.

**Barolo in brief.** Barolo is made from [Nebbiolo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nebbiolo) in the hills south-west of [Alba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alba,_Piedmont), and is often described as one of Italy's greatest wines, with aromas of "tar and roses". It must age at least 36 months after the harvest, 18 of them in wood, and traditionally needed ten years or more to soften ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barolo)).

Antonio Galloni gives the 2012 as a blend of six vineyards: Liste and Terlo in Barolo, two parcels in Mosconi in Monforte, and Gabutti and Baudana in Serralunga ([Trialto, Vinous review](https://trialto.kork.ca/en/press-reviews/vinous-barolo-via-nuova-2012)). Trialto is the BC importer.

**The vintage.** [Jancis Robinson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jancis_Robinson)'s [Piemonte vintage chart](https://www.jancisrobinson.com/learn/vintages/piemonte) says an unusually hot summer "unexpectedly resulted in Nebbiolos with low alcohol levels and high acidity". Cool weather into April delayed budbreak, hail destroyed vineyards in Novello in July, and August heat above 40°C shut the vines down until late-August rain restarted ripening; a dry autumn allowed a late harvest. "Overall a light vintage but with several excellent wines on the top level", the best showing "acidic nerve, balance and freshness".

**What the critics say for 2012.**
- **[Vinous](https://vinous.com): 95** (Antonio Galloni, March 2016, via [Trialto](https://trialto.kork.ca/en/press-reviews/vinous-barolo-via-nuova-2012)). "A wine of extraordinary precision" with "stunning vibrancy and energy": dark cherry, cherry pit, blood orange, orange peel, exotic spice and mint in "a chiseled Barolo that bristles with energy"; super-classic, mid-weight, with knock-out aromatics and fabulous balance. "This is compelling juice."
- **[CellarTracker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CellarTracker) community: 93.0** (from your CellarTracker list).
- (Other critics' notes for the 2012 were on pages I couldn't read, so I've left their scores out.)

**How it's drinking now.** In October 2026 the wine is fourteen years old. Your CellarTracker list gives a window of 2020 to 2027. A lighter, fresher vintage, this is at its peak now: cherry, orange peel, spice, roses and tar. Drink it over the next few years; decant an hour ahead.

**Serving.** Decant Barolo an hour or two ahead; older bottles need only a gentle decant off the sediment. Serve at about 16 to 18°C in a large glass.

**Food.** Barolo belongs with Piedmontese food: [tajarin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tagliolini) with butter and white truffle, brasato al Barolo (beef braised in the wine), [vitello tonnato](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vitello_tonnato), roast game, or aged cheeses like [Castelmagno](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Castelmagno_cheese).

**Value and where to buy.** Chiara Boschis's wines are easy to find here: ZYN has the Via Nuova 2021 at $160, the Cannubi 2020 at $261 and a Dolcetto d'Alba at $39.90; BSW Liquor has the Via Nuova 2020 at $175, Cannubi 2020 at $260 and Mosconi 2020 at $185.

**From the history books**
- **Tar and roses.** Barolo's production code has always required hillside vineyards; the 2010 revision went further, excluding valley floors, flat and humid land and full north-facing slopes ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barolo)).
- **The modernists.** Traditional Barolo spent at least three weeks on its skins and years in large casks; to appeal to modern tastes, several producers began shortening macerations and using new French barriques ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barolo)), the movement Chiara Boschis joined in 1990.

**Barolo through the ages**
- **Sweet before it was dry?** It was long believed Barolo was a sweet wine until the mid-19th century, because Nebbiolo ripens so late that cold cellars stopped the fermentation, and that [Count Cavour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Camillo_Benso,_Count_of_Cavour), mayor of [Grinzane Cavour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grinzane_Cavour), brought in the Frenchman Louis Oudart to make it dry. Research by Kerin O'Keefe credits instead Paolo Francesco Staglieno, Cavour's oenologist at Grinzane from 1836 to 1841, whose "Staglieno method" fermented the wine dry ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barolo)).
- **"The wine of kings, the king of wines."** The new dry Barolo became a favourite of the nobility of [Turin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turin) and the ruling [House of Savoy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_of_Savoy) ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barolo)).
- **From merchants to growers.** By the mid-20th century large merchants dominated, blending grapes from across the zone; in the 1960s growers began bottling their own wines and single vineyards, and in 1980 Barolo became one of Italy's first DOCGs, with Barbaresco and Brunello ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barolo)).
- **The Barolo wars.** In the 1970s and 80s a group of producers, led by Ceretto, Paolo Cordero di Montezemolo, Elio Altare and Renato Ratti, began making more modern Barolo, with macerations of days rather than weeks and small new oak barrels, to tame Nebbiolo's harsh tannins. Traditionalists kept to long macerations and years in large casks ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barolo)).

**Curious details**
- **A mortgage for a dream.** Chiara convinced her parents to mortgage the family to buy E. Pira while she was still at university ([Skurnik Wines](https://www.skurnik.com/e-pira-chiara-boschis-now-a-family-affair/)).
- **The next generation.** Giorgio and Daniella's daughters, Beatrice, Elena and Vittoria, are already working at the "new" family winery, giving Barolo another generation of women winemakers ([Skurnik Wines](https://www.skurnik.com/e-pira-chiara-boschis-now-a-family-affair/)).
